title: Building Your Claude Toolkit
description: Assemble a personal toolkit of reusable prompts, workflows, and best practices that make Claude a permanent part of your daily productivity.

data.text: The difference between a casual Claude user and a power user is not raw intelligence — it is a toolkit. Power users have a library of proven prompts, know which model to use for which task, and have workflows that turn Claude from a novelty into a reliable daily tool. This lesson helps you build that toolkit.

Start a document (Notion, Google Docs, or even a text file) where you collect prompts that work well. Every time you craft a prompt that produces great output, save it. Over time, you will build a personal library of prompts tailored to your specific work, audience, and style. This is one of the highest-ROI activities you can do with Claude.

data.title: Start your library with these essential templates:
items: Email draft — specify recipient, purpose, tone, and key points
Document summary — paste text, ask for key points and action items
Code review — paste code, ask for improvements and potential bugs
Brainstorming — ask for 10 ideas with pros and cons for each
Learning explanation — ask Claude to explain a concept at your level
Editing — paste text, specify the type of edit needed

items.hint: Notion, Google Docs, or Obsidian work well

items.text: Set a custom instruction for your primary use case
Identify your top 3 use cases and optimize prompts for each
items.hint: Quality over quantity — master a few prompts deeply

items.text: Bookmark the Claude API documentation for advanced use
items.hint: Even if you do not code now, understanding the API helps
Keep hallucination and cutoff awareness top of mind

items.text: Set up one integration with a tool you use daily
items.hint: Slack, Notion, or email are good starting points

data.text: When to Use Claude vs. Other Tools

A mature Claude user knows when Claude is the right tool and when another tool is better. Claude excels at long documents, careful writing, and nuanced analysis. Use Perplexity for live research with citations. Use ChatGPT for image generation and code execution. Use Gemini when working inside Google Workspace. Knowing when to switch is the hallmark of an advanced AI user.

data.text: Your Claude toolkit should evolve. Every month, review your prompt library — remove prompts that no longer work, add new ones you have discovered, and refine existing ones. Follow Anthropic's blog and documentation to learn about new features like extended context windows, new models, and updated API capabilities. The Claude ecosystem evolves quickly, and staying current keeps your toolkit effective.

data.title: Start small, build over time
data.text: Do not try to build a comprehensive toolkit in one day. Start with one prompt you use frequently, one custom instruction, and one integration. Add one new element per week. In three months, you will have a toolkit that makes Claude feel like a natural extension of how you work.

data.title: Building your toolkit
points: Start a prompt library and add prompts that work well
Set custom instructions for your primary use case
Know which tool to use for which task — Claude is not always the answer
Set up at least one integration with a tool you use daily
Review and refine your toolkit monthly as the ecosystem evolves
